purpose: Scale accurate monster identity across hundreds of creatures while keeping production recipes tiny. Broad family DNA, species identity, variant recipe, and page scene are separate layers.
resolution_order: explicit recipe overrides only for true variant differences
page scene recipe owns the exact environment/action/props
rules: Broad family profiles own reusable anatomy and anti-drift intelligence shared by multiple species or variants.
Species identity profiles own canonical creature-specific anatomy and may inherit a broad family profile.
Monster recipes own only ID/name/profile references plus true variant deltas.
Page recipes own the exact habitat, composition, props, support, interaction, and story moment.
Known failure modes must be active generation/review corrections, not passive documentation.
Identity data must not contain page-only scene requirements such as a particular pillar, pedestal, key, victim, room, trap, or altar.
Reusable scenery must never be copied into monster recipes or identity profiles.
Environment-fit metadata is planning-only once a page environment profile has been selected.
New production monsters should use schema v4; schema v1-v3 are migration compatibility only.
scalability_rule: Hundreds of monster recipes remain tiny pointers plus true variant deltas. Reusable anatomy lives in family/species identity profiles; reusable scenery lives only in the environment engine; exact action and props live only in the page recipe.

monster_may_define: variant-specific environment preferences when truly unique
environment_ownership.rule: If a visual element could be reused by another creature in the same place, it belongs in the universal environment engine: family/profile/component/overlay system.

identity_profile_engine.purpose: Species-level canonical identity that may inherit a broad family profile but does not own a specific page composition.
identity_profile_engine.fallback_rule: For simple species with no separate species file, identity_profile may resolve directly to an existing family profile.
ownership: species-specific silhouette, anatomy, body plan, appendages, surface treatment, and scale
species-specific accuracy checks and known failure corrections
species-level render mode such as single, swarm, amorphous, object, fragment, or split form
forbidden_ownership: one page's exact victim, key, pillar, pedestal, altar, or trap
one page's exact pose or story interaction

prompt_budget.rule: Generation receives one concise authoritative MONSTER BRIEF plus a small set of identity anchors and drift corrections; full catalog prose remains available for QA.

render_identity.rule: Subject mode describes how the creature should read as a coloring-book focal subject and prevents one-monster composition rules from breaking swarms, animated objects, oozes, detached limbs, or split forms.

anatomy_engine.purpose: Structured anatomy supplements prose for creatures whose correctness depends on counts or unusual body plans.
anatomy_engine.rule: Use structured anatomy when limb count, wings, tentacles, segments, multiple bodies, or unusual support are identity-critical. Prose remains authoritative for nuance.
